messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency SLO breach on serving-cluster-us-west-2 (streaming) — paging cheng (oncall) @cheng. service: text-streaming, metric: p99=2.8s (SLO=1.0s), affected nodes: 3 GPUs, severity: P1
cheng (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing context and paging SRE.
maya (sre): I'm awake, joining. any customer-facing impact known?
eva (support): Support tools show ~12 customer sessions with streaming stalls in the last 5m. One enterprise tenant reporting partial timeouts in iframe. ticket #9872.
alex (platform): I'm seeing an uptick in ECC correctable errors on node-ops-gpu-14/15/19. fan curves spiking; thermal readings show GPU Tjunction trending to 92C.
lucas (ml eng): Streaming stalls match KV cache misses and GPU stall traces — NVLINK errors visible in dmesg on those nodes.
cheng (oncall): OK plan: 1) remove affected GPUs from routing (failover to spare capacity). 2) drain streaming sessions and route to fallback replicas (lower-throughput). 3) notify customers via status page if impact expands.
maya (sre): I'll start the evacuation now. alex, can you confirm graceful drain command and fallback route name?
alex (platform): run: `redwoodctl drain-node node-ops-gpu-14 --grace-period 60s --stream-fallback=streaming-low-cpu` I'll kick that on 14/15/19 in parallel. using canary to avoid overload.
cheng (oncall): execute and monitor. +confirm when each drain completes.
(alex runs command)
alex (platform): started drain on node-ops-gpu-14 (cmd id c-42). hooking KV cache warmers to fallback.
vendor-ops-bot: Hardware vendor notified: ticket V-2026 opened. Observed ECC correctable error spike; suggested firmware probe and fan curve check.
maya (sre): Drain complete on 14, p99 dropped to 1.6s but still above SLO. started drain on 15.
lucas (ml eng): For in-flight streams, added server-side prefix caching to reduce token compute; this should shave ~200-300ms for common prompts.
eva (support): Customer-facing update drafted: "We are experiencing streaming delays for some sessions in US-WEST; mitigation in progress; no data loss reported." Ready to post if we see further regressions.
sam (sales): We have an active demo with EnterpriseX at 10:00 PST that may be affected, pinging product to suggest reschedule if impact persists.
maya (sre): Node-ops-gpu-15 drain finished. Node-ops-gpu-19 showing intermittent ECC bursts; cooling fans at 85% but Tjunction still 90C. considering quarantine.
alex (platform): Quarantine 19 via `redwoodctl isolate-node node-ops-gpu-19 --reason=ECC-thermal` and spin up dedicated fallback capacity on dedicated-pool-b.
cheng (oncall): Isolate done. Spinning fallback replicas now. Observed p99 at 0.98s after fallback capacity came online. Good.
lucas (ml eng): Note: fallback uses smaller batch sizes and lower kv_cache size, output quality unchanged for simple prompts. will run regen checks on complex evals.
eva (support): Posted status update. CustomerX support ticket updated with workaround instructions to refresh stream session.
vendor-ops-bot: Vendor suggests scheduling firmware update and replacing GPU if ECC correctables persist after cooling test. Next steps: hardware bench tomorrow AM.
maya (sre): Root cause hypothesis: hardware degradation + thermal management causing correctable ECC spikes -> GPU microstalls -> long tail in streaming. Mitigation: quarantine, fallback capacity, prefix caching, batch tuning.
cheng (oncall): Post-incident actions: 1) collect nvlink/dmesg logs from 14/15/19. 2) run hardware stress + fan-profile repro. 3) schedule replacement or firmware update. 4) add automated rule to detect rapid correctable error ramp and preemptively evacuate. Assigning to alex and vendor-ops.
alex (platform): Ack. I'll gather logs and open replacement order if vendor confirms.
sam (sales): Please keep me posted on demo status — thx.
lucas (ml eng): I'll run a quick eval on degraded vs fallback model to quantify QoL diff; will share metrics.
maya (sre): We should also update ops playbook: add explicit eviction threshold for ECC correctables >500/min for >2m -> auto-drain.
cheng (oncall): For now severity -> downgraded to P2 since fallback restored SLO and customer impact limited. keeping thread open for follow-ups.
eva (support): closing customer ticket as workaround applied, will reopen if issue resumes. thanks all.
incident-bot: Incident status changed: Mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owners: cheng (oncall), alex (platform), vendor-ops. Tags: hardware, thermal, ECC, streaming
cheng (oncall): logging followup doc in #incidents-postmortems and will create a postmortem draft. If anyone has screenshots/log fragments, drop them here.
lucas (ml eng): dropping sample trace: `gpu stall at 0x7f2e... nvlink_retry_count=24` (pasted to the log stash).
maya (sre): thumbs. good rapid coordination. closing loop with vendor tomorrow.
